subject: What is the actual statistical test behind the morphol.disparity function in geomorph?

messages.author: f207a911f8d70cb3
messages.subject: What is the actual statistical test behind the morphol.disparity function in geomorph?
parts:
Dear Geomorph Group,

I am writing up the results of a geomorphic morphometric analysis for publication. For this study, I examined the difference between the variances of different categories (i.e., does a certain category occupy a greater morphospace and is this significant) using the morphol.disparity function in geomorph.

However, after submitting the paper, the reviewers came back to me and said they wanted more information as to exact what test was used to compare the different variances between the groups. I cannot seem to find what the actual statistical basis is for the morphol.disparity function. I checked over the vignette in the help function and it does not give any description as to what the actual mechanism the function uses to compare variances is or what it might be called. I know it calculates variances and how it does this but how the function gets a p-value from those variances is unclear. I was wondering if anyone here knew the mathematical basis as to how this function works.

Sincerely,
Russell

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] What is the actual statistical test behind the morphol.disparity function in geomorph?
parts:
Russell,

 

As per the help file:  ‘Absolute differences in Procrustes variances are test statistics that can be used to test differences in morphological disparity among groups.’

 

Statistically, this is analogous in logic to the numerator of a t-test (or T^2 test). No difference between groups is a difference score of zero, and larger absolute values represent greater difference between groups. The difference for disparity is that rather than comparing means, one is comparing variances. Significance is then assessed via permutation.

 

Dean
